adoption.notes: Implements the Producer Time members and the action_log record members in the sensor_history and action_log exports and the Tier 3 request, and vendors this version's export-rows corpus. It does not claim this version and pages action_log by count. From 97649a76 it checks every subscription's payload against its family's maximum before parse and bounds each family's rate, counting and logging each refusal by family and reason, and by size class for an oversized payload. Its export request bound is a bucket that starts full with 10 requests and gains 2 a second, judged at arrival on the monotonic clock: the export-rate floor this version now states. It answers at most 4 export requests at once, also this version's floor, and a request refused for a slot has already spent its rate token. No runtime test pins either value yet. From 97649a76 it keeps each replay key until its envelope is stale or replay_ttl_ms from receipt, whichever is later, and persists the keys while persistent_replay_cache is true, its default. From ad4a1cc8 it answers no export request whose envelope is not verified, and an inbound evidence message its executor is too busy to take is left undecided with its replay key still recorded. From d9f66378 it admits every gateway payload under the Payload Member Rule before any member is read or its envelope verified. From 6b597521 it admits the health reading's member names only in the element objects of an export response's root items array, and refuses a case variant of one inside such an item as case_variant_member. From 0de8340d it implements Envelope Freshness and Replay, checking the signature and topic-device first, then stale_timestamp, future_timestamp, before_replay_floor and replay_detected in that order. Every dropped or evicted key raises a replay floor past its signing time, stored with the held keys in one transaction, and each start takes the greater of the stored floor and its start clock; a full cache evicts the key with the smallest signing time rather than refusing an authentic envelope. No rotation lowers its floor or drops a held key, as this version now requires. From cf622538 it runs the replay corpus vendored at c1557a0 through its authenticator with no case declined. It reads a floor an earlier run stored while persistent_replay_cache is false, and never writes it. While its replay store cannot be opened, read or written, at start or later in a run, it refuses every envelope that passes the signature and topic-device checks as before_replay_floor, drops no held key and writes no floor, and the refusal survives a restart. A raise that cannot be stored keeps its key held, and a key that cannot be stored is refused. Its tests drive the floor_unreadable and floor_read events through a real store lock. From 6b597521 it runs the replay corpus vendored at e081330 with no change. Its node heartbeat takes last_seen_ms from its wall clock when built, the fallback included, and sends gateway_seen_ms as 0, as this version now states. It does not check that clock against this version's range for last_seen_ms, 1 to 9007199254740991, so a wall clock at 0 or past the ceiling publishes a last_seen_ms the gateway is to refuse. From 0de8340d it signs every gateway envelope it sends, the node heartbeat, reasoning requests, export responses and inbound evidence acknowledgements, from one signing clock whose values are claimed ahead in the state database. That clock refuses to sign, never blocking, once its claim is used up or a value would run more than a reservation ahead of the wall clock, and health then reads degraded; an in-memory database is refused at start in staging and production with gateway.auth enabled. From 4ea8bcfa it vendors the health-transition corpus and its producer baselines and tests that every health export snapshot it builds writes critical as a JSON boolean; the corpus is the gateway's to prove. It vendored this version's corpora at 45eb5c8 at 0de8340d, at 169e061 at 4ea8bcfa, at c1557a0 at cf622538, and at e081330 at 6b597521. It has no release, and its evidence is host tests and CI, not deployed interoperability with a gateway, resource budgets on target hardware, or HIL.

From 84489bb it implements Payload Size: one table of family maxima, every subscription bound to a family, the length checked in the broker's message wrapper before anything else, a refusal unanswered, stateless and logged by family and size class, every required reply it produces within the 4096-byte floor, an over-maximum reasoning or enrichment response replaced by response_too_large, no export request over its maximum published, request_id held to its pattern, inbound evidence published as canonical JSON with its acknowledgement matched on the canonical bytes, and an authority artifact over the hop refused at staging as an unrecognised outcome. It offers no setting that lowers a maximum. From 84489bb it implements Payload Volume, with per-device message rates and, from 243ebb7, per-device byte budgets for each received family, unconfigured device segments sharing one bucket, and site health reporting payload_too_large and volume_dropped for each family; an inbound evidence acknowledgement that decides nothing, or an export response whose request is no longer pending, records no replay state. From 243ebb7 it implements the Payload Member Rule in the broker wrapper after size and rate and before any handler, admits a decrypted export plaintext the same way, refuses at staging, as an unrecognised outcome after routing, a correctly routed authority artifact whose inbound message the rule refuses, and publishes no inbound message the rule refuses. From bfb9662 it implements the Export Auth Envelope: an export response is verified under its waiting request's device_id and request_id before delivery, one that does not verify is dropped and logged and records no replay key while the request keeps waiting, each request waits at most 30 seconds from its publish, and an export reads at most 100 pages. From a0dd23c it implements Envelope Freshness and Replay, refusing stale, future, before_replay_floor and replay in that order, keeping keys until stale and raising the floor at every drop, and runs the replay corpus through its verifier; it signs every envelope outside the evidence path from one message signing clock with its mark in gateway.state_directory under gateway-config/v2. From ec162f4 a write of that mark that never returns no longer blocks its signers or its shutdown: it opens an episode, as gateway-config/v2 requires. From 0d49ff5 it hands an export response over only while its request's wait has not expired, so a late response completes nothing and records no replay key, fails an export as malformed when a page that verifies lacks an envelope member, drops unverified a signed page that lacks request_id or device_id, the export then failing at its time bound, and paces exports per device at 1.6 a second with bursts of 8, below the runtime's admission rate and within the export-rate floor this version now states. It sets no bound of its own on export requests outstanding to a device; its current callers, one debounced health and posture fetch and the weekly report's requests one at a time, keep at most 2, within the in-flight floor; a new caller would need its own bound. From 1cbdbcd it reads a health export's severity under Reading `status` while runtimes adopt runtime-health/v4, once the response has verified and against the requested device, never reading ok from an absent status, and holds a device to the projection once it has served one. In site health it raises a node's status by its export severity and never lowers it, unobserved nodes included; it does not yet carry export_severity, which this version now defines. It does not yet hold the export-response members this version adds from the health reading, so it admits their case variants. From 373794c it handles reasoning and enrichment requests off the broker's ordered delivery, and handles outbound carriages and inbound acknowledgements one at a time per device in arrival order, holding each family's messages at most at its ingress burst. A message over that bound is dropped unanswered and counted as volume_dropped, but only after the Payload Member Rule has parsed it, where Payload Volume drops without reading past the size check, a deviation the gateway has still to remove. From 78d4d3d its CI runs the race detector and measures its courier and broker timing tests against their oracles; no production code changed. From 72cfd01 site health judges a node's liveness, eviction and staleness on the gateway's monotonic receipt age alone, and a node is stale when no heartbeat has advanced its last_seen_ms past the previous heartbeat's within the TTL. It stamps gateway_seen_ms as the wall-clock receipt, for display only, and admits but never reads a producer-supplied gateway_seen_ms, as this version's Site Health liveness rule now requires. It still refuses a heartbeat whose last_seen_ms is more than 5 minutes ahead of its wall clock, which this version forbids, and decodes last_seen_ms and gateway_seen_ms as 64-bit integers, so it admits either above 9007199254740991, and a negative gateway_seen_ms, where this version refuses them. From d4e4b4d no GW-6 escalation waits on its log destination, and site health reports the gateway degraded while its own heartbeat is not going out; no wire changed. It vendored this version's payload size, payload members and replay corpora at 404cbcb at a0dd23c, at c2bed1a at ec162f4, and at 169e061 at 1cbdbcd, with the health-transition corpus and its baselines. It has no release, and its evidence is host tests and CI, not deployed interoperability with a runtime, resource budgets on target hardware, or HIL.

notes: Created by the baseline audit of gateway-api/v1 as the destination of its three semantic post-freeze hunks: the gateway serves only configured devices, the reasoning response carries a required `device_id` and the runtime refuses an invalid `action_tier`, and an explicit `escalate_to: gateway` returns a gateway-unavailable result instead of falling back. The text is v1's as it stood on main before the audit removed those edits from v1; v1 also keeps the additive families (runtime node heartbeat, enrichment, evidence carriage, exports) as they stood. This version carries their successors where runtime-health/v4 changes them: the runtime node heartbeat gains the `critical` status, the enlarged `degradation_reasons` vocabulary and its validation steps, and the `health` export becomes the remote health projection. The runtime shipped the response rule in v1.0.0 and will be recorded here once it claims this version. Amended in place while amendable: sensor readings carry `producer_time`, so a receipt sent in `timestamp` is never read as a measurement, and `action_log` rows carry `record_kind`, `record_key` and `contributed_to` in a stable page order. Payload Size bounds every topic's payload length before any parse, and Payload Volume bounds each receiver's processing rate and state; the maxima count `device_id` at the bound runtime-config/v2 declares and `request_id` at 128 characters, every required reply fits the 4096-byte floor, and an inbound evidence message is published in canonical form. The gateway and the runtime each enforce both on their main branches. The runtime logs its refusals by family and does not yet report them in runtime-health/v4's mqtt_ingress block, which Payload Volume now names. The degradation_reasons vocabulary now holds firmware_signing_domains_undeclared, which the gateway refuses in a heartbeat, so no runtime names it yet; the gateway's health client also drops the projection's undeclared_device_count and mqtt_ingress block, and its own mqtt_ingress posture stays separate from them. Payload Volume also sets floors on the runtime's export request bounds, a bucket of 10 gaining 2 a second and 4 answered at once, which the gateway never exceeds, with publish on the topic granted to the gateway's broker identity alone. The runtime's bounds meet them; the gateway's pacing meets the rate floor, and its callers stay within the in-flight floor without a bound of their own. Export Auth Envelope defines the export envelope: a runtime does not answer an export request whose envelope is not verified, and a gateway drops an unverified export response and bounds its wait for every export request, which it adopts first. The gateway and the runtime each enforce it on their main branches. Envelope Freshness and Replay keeps each replay key until its envelope is stale, with replay_ttl_ms only a lower bound, and adds a replay floor: every dropped key raises it past that envelope's signing time, every start raises it to the start clock, and an envelope signed below it is refused as before_replay_floor. Every sender signs each attempt afresh. The gateway and the runtime each keep keys until stale and keep a floor on their main branches.
